About the Dental Terminology event

Dental Terminology is a Health Science event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing.

Eleven in-depth lessons following the HOSA Dental Terminology test plan, with labeled skull, tooth, cavity and radiograph models, an interactive tooth chart, a nerve-block simulator, emergency cases and spelling drills for the tiebreaker.

Dental Terminology lessons

Unit 1 · Head, neck and tooth anatomy

Skull, muscles of mastication, the oral cavity, tooth tissues, surfaces and numbering systems.

  1. Head and neck anatomy 25 min

    A patient grimaces when opening wide, clicks when chewing and points just in front of the ear. Another has a numb lower lip three days after a wisdom tooth extraction. A dental professional who knows the bones, joints…

  2. Tooth anatomy, morphology and numbering 25 min

    On a chart, “MOD #30” and “DL caries on #3” are complete sentences to a dental professional: which tooth, which surfaces and what problem. Behind that shorthand is detailed knowledge of tooth tissues, surfaces, ridges…

Unit 2 · Comprehensive care and specialties

Test plan: 30%, the largest domain. General dentistry, examination and every recognized specialty.

  1. General dentistry, examination and the dental office 25 min

    A new patient visit includes a medical history, vital signs, a head and neck exam, radiographs, a periodontal charting, a hard tissue charting, a cleaning and a treatment plan. Each step has its own vocabulary and…

  2. Specialties I: endodontics, periodontics, orthodontics and pediatric dentistry 25 min

    A lingering toothache that keeps a patient up at night, bleeding gums and loose teeth, crooked teeth that make chewing difficult, a frightened four-year-old with decay: each problem sends a patient to a different…

  3. Specialties II: oral surgery, prosthodontics, implants and cosmetic dentistry 25 min

    A teenager’s impacted wisdom teeth are pressing on the second molars. A retiree wants to replace a missing molar and is choosing between a bridge, a partial denture and an implant. A bride wants whiter, more even teeth…

Unit 3 · Instruments and restorations

Instrument families, tray order, cavity preparation and direct and indirect restorations.

  1. Dental instruments 20 min

    A tray of twelve shiny instruments looks alike to a new student, yet each has a precise name, design and order of use. Pass the wrong one and the procedure stalls. The test even asks what a “cowhorn” is. Learning…

  2. Tooth restorations and cavity preparation 25 min

    A patient asks why her new filling is tooth-colored when her old one was silver, why her friend got a crown instead of a filling, and why the dentist needed impressions for a “porcelain onlay.” The answers depend on how…

Unit 4 · Laboratory and radiography

Impression materials, gypsum, waxes and lab procedures; X-ray production, interpretation, technique errors and safety.

  1. Dental laboratory materials and procedures 25 min

    An alginate impression is perfect when it comes out of the mouth, but left on the counter for an hour it shrinks, and the model poured from it no longer fits. Laboratory work depends on chemistry: water ratios, setting…

  2. Dental radiography 25 min

    On a bitewing radiograph, a faint dark triangle just below the contact point between two molars reveals decay that no explorer could reach. A bright white blob shows an old amalgam, and a gray line shows where the bone…

Unit 5 · Pharmacology, pain management and emergencies

Local anesthetics, injections, sedation and dental drugs; medical and dental emergencies.

  1. Dental pharmacology and pain management 25 min

    Before a filling, the dentist pairs 2% lidocaine with 1:100,000 epinephrine, aspirates, injects slowly and waits. Afterward the patient gets ibuprofen, not an opioid, and a reminder not to chew on her numb lip. Every…

  2. Emergency care in the dental office 25 min

    A teenage patient sits up after an injection, turns pale, starts sweating and slumps in the chair. Fainting is the most common emergency in a dental office, and most emergencies are preventable or quickly reversible…

Dental Terminology practice tests

Sample Dental Terminology questions

1. Which radiograph shows large areas of the upper or lower arch, useful for impacted teeth or jaw fractures?

  1. Bitewing
  2. Occlusal
  3. Periapical
  4. Cephalometric
Show answer

B. Occlusal

The patient bites on the receptor, which captures a broad view of the arch.

2. A thin shell of porcelain bonded to the front of a tooth to improve its appearance is called a:

  1. Crown
  2. Veneer
  3. Inlay
  4. Bridge
Show answer

B. Veneer

Veneers are a cosmetic treatment covering the facial surface. A crown covers the entire tooth.

3. For which patients may antibiotic premedication be recommended before certain dental procedures?

  1. All patients over age 50
  2. All patients with braces
  3. Patients with prosthetic valves
  4. Patients with a common cold
Show answer

C. Patients with prosthetic valves

Premedication helps prevent infective endocarditis in high-risk patients, such as those with prosthetic valves or a history of endocarditis.
